name: b-crosshatch-hospital-dusk
prompt: Portrait pen-and-ink newspaper cartoon drawing, black India ink on warm off-white newsprint, built entirely from fine crosshatched lines with confident thick contours and no grey wash or colour. A slatted wooden park bench with curly cast-iron ends sits square to the viewer at eye level, the whole bench and both figures filling the lower half of the frame. On the left a portly, smug rich gentleman from a century ago, completely unchanged by time: tall silk top hat, tight buttoned waistcoat stretched over his belly with a watch chain, frock coat, striped trousers, white spats, one leg crossed, chin raised, eyes half-lidded, flicking a gloved hand outward in a lazy brush-off toward his neighbour. On the right a young nurse in modern hospital scrubs with a lanyard and ID card, chunky trainers, slumped against the backrest, eyes closed with exhaustion, both hands around a paper takeaway coffee cup resting on her knee. Behind them a present-day park at dusk drawn in the same old pen technique: a wheelie-style litter bin beside the bench, a slim modern lamp post with a phone-charging socket, bare trees, and beyond the trees a tall hospital tower block rendered in dense layered hatching, its many lit windows left as small clean white rectangles in the black. The hatching thickens toward the ground and the tower, so the light is fading evening glow from behind the building; the top quarter of the image is open pale sky with only the lightest sparse strokes, left empty. Strict monochrome ink only, no lettering, no words, no signature, no speech balloons anywhere in the picture.
